data.long_meaning: The name Ekaparna means 'One–Bearing'. In Hindu mythology, Ekaparna refers to Lord Shiva, who carries the goddess Parvati on his shoulders. This name symbolizes love, compassion, and the divine union of Shiva and Parvati. The name Ekaparna carries the meaning “One–Bearing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekaparna usually hope their child will grow to embody one–bearing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine union and love
data.etymology: Ekaparna belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One–Bearing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekaparna total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Ekaparna is commonly associated with Lord Shiva, the god of destruction. He is depicted as carrying the goddess Parvati on his shoulders, signifying their eternal love and unity. This image represents the concept of Shiva–Shakti, where the male and female forces are inseparable and in harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: Ekaparna symbolizes sacrifice, devotion, and companionship. It represents the idea of carrying the burden of another, emphasizing the deep bond between two souls. The spiritual significance of this name also comes from Lord Shiva's role as the embodiment of transience and change. Therefore, Ekaparna's name can inspire individuals to embrace change, remain devoted to their loved ones, and find inner strength during challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ekaparna symbolizes unity and perfection, represented by the solitary fruit on the palasa tree in Hindu mythology. This name evokes the ideals of being self-sufficient and complete in one's own being.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu god Ekaparna is a form of Lord Vishnu. He is also known as the 'One-Thousand-Petaled Lotus' form of Vishnu. This form of Vishnu is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Bhagavata Purana.
Another reference to Ekaparna can be found in the Mahabharata, where the god is described as having thousand petals on his lotus feet, and it is believed that he grants boons to his devotees.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, circa 4th Century BCE - 4th Century CE
